headline: When Your Shower Renovation Goes Wrong
articleBody: A new shower can be a refreshing upgrade, but it’s incredibly frustrating when things don't go according to plan. If your shower renovation is experiencing plumbing problems, recognizing when to call in the experts can prevent minor annoyances from becoming major headaches. One of the most obvious signs is persistent leaking. Whether it's from the showerhead, faucet handles, or a puddle on the floor outside the shower, any leak needs immediate attention. Even a small leak can lead to water damage within walls or flooring. Another common issue is inconsistent water temperature or pressure. If your water suddenly goes cold, or the pressure drops significantly, it indicates a problem with the mixing valve, water lines, or even your water heater connection. Don't try to troubleshoot these complex systems yourself. You should also watch out for slow drainage. If your new shower pan takes too long to drain, it suggests a blockage or an improperly sloped drain line, which can cause water to pool and potentially lead to overflows or mildew growth. Lastly, if you notice any unusual smells, like a persistent musty odor, it could be a sign of hidden leaks or mold growth behind the walls, which requires prompt investigation. For any of these issues, it's best to bring in a professional plumber.
